childs.title: General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System
childs.author: J. Rives Childs
childs.edition_year_evidence: Lasry et al. cite the Aegean Park Press edition as 2000. The inspected imprint page in this scan does not itself print a publication year; the cover's 2002 B 3922 is a library accession/call label.
childs.technical_paper_date_evidence: The main report reproduces the text and examples of General Solution for the ADFGVX Cipher System, whose separate US Government Printing Office title page explicitly prints Washington: 1934 (source nsa_general_solution). This is a publication date, not an asserted original composition date.
childs.historical_manuscript_date: The editor's introduction says the Childs paper was written after World War I and was later published in part in the 1930s; it gives no precise composition year.
childs.kind: Historical report containing the intercept logs and key appendix
childs.page_convention: For the intercept log and key appendix used here, printed page n is PDF page n+3 in the 248-page public scan. The initial frontmatter and omitted blank pages do not follow this rule.

nsa_summary.author: J. R. Childs, with added notes by H. C. Skinner and William F. Friedman
nsa_summary.composition_evidence: The foreword says Childs wrote the report about December 1918; it separately identifies added notes 7 and 12, the latter prepared in January 1919.
nsa_summary.date_locator: Publication year on PDF page 5; foreword date and composition statement on PDF page 7.
nsa_summary.kind: Declassified historical report; a different work from the complete Childs book

nsa_general_solution.title: General Solution for the ADFGVX Cipher System
nsa_general_solution.corporate_author: War Department, Signal Intelligence Section, War Plans and Training Division
nsa_general_solution.publisher: United States Government Printing Office, Washington
nsa_general_solution.locator: Register No.129; publication year on PDF page4; solution attribution in printed page2 footnote1
nsa_general_solution.kind: The earlier technical paper reproduced in the opening section of the Aegean Park Press volume; distinct from the 1919 Childs manuscript and the 1935 German Military Ciphers report
nsa_general_solution.attribution_note: The paper credits the general solution to F. B. Rowlett, S. Kullback and A. Sinkov, and cites Childs's earlier report for wartime special-case methods. The Aegean title page describes its text as derived from a paper by Childs; these statements should not be collapsed into sole authorship of every method.
